question: to the Commission Ignazio Roberto Marino (Verts/ALE) Subject:

In its judgment of 5 February 2026 in case C-810/24 (Urban Vision), the Court of Justice of the European Union ruled that the mechanism enabling the promoter of a project financing procedure to adjust its offer to match the top offer, in order to be awarded the contract, was incompatible with Article 3(1) of Directive 2014/23/EU. The Italian Council of State applied those principles in judgment No 3805 of 14 May 2026. By way of public notice issued on 29 May 2025, the Italian Ministry of Infrastructure launched the concession procedure for the Rome-Latina intermodal corridor (between Tor de’ Cenci and Latina Borgo Piave). On the basis of paragraph 7, if the promoter is not awarded the contract, it may nevertheless exercise a pre-emption right and be awarded the contract, provided it complies with the same terms as the successful tenderer. On 4 June 2026, the matter was put to the Italian Chamber of Deputies in a question for immediate reply. In view of the above: 1.
Is the Commission aware of this procedure and the conditions benefiting the promoter?
In light of judgment C-810/24, does it deem this procedure compatible with Article 3(1) of Directive 2014/23/EU?
Will it seek clarification from the Italian authorities and, if necessary, take steps to ensure full application of the judgment?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.9.2026) As a general rule, the Commission does not examine the details of individual procedures, such as the one referred to by the Honourable Member, as Member States are better placed to investigate individual tendering procedures. The Commission notes that national courts and review bodies referred to in the directives on remedies in public procurement1 are primarily responsible to assess whether, according to the relevant legal and factual circumstances of each individual case, contracting authorities and contracting entities respected their obligations under EU law. Nonetheless, the Commission refers back to its reply to written question P-001533/20262 and recalls that as confirmed by the Court of Justice of the European Union in the judgment cited by the Honourable Member, the provision of a pre-emption right in favour of the promoter such as the one that was foreseen in the national legislation at stake is contrary to the principles of non-discrimination and equal treatment, as enshrined in the EU public procurement rules, and that preliminary rulings are binding both on the referring court and on all courts in Member States. However, it is primarily for the authorities of the Member State concerned to take the general or specific measures necessary to ensure that EU law is complied with within that State.
1 Directive 89/665/EEC and Directive 92/13/EEC, as amended by Directive 2007/66/EC and Directive
